Subject: Exploring a switch from monthly billing to a yearly reserve (questions)

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. Brightpath is evaluating moving our LLM consumption from month-to-month to a yearly reserve to get better unit economics and simplify our forecasting. A few quick questions so we can get internal approvals: 

- If we convert our current spend (~$20k/mo average over the last 6 months) to a 12-month reserve, what discount bands would Redwood offer for year 1 and year 2 (if we do a 2-yr commit)?
- Can unused credit in year 1 roll forward to year 2, or do you allow a true-up? How do you handle under-commit risk?
- We need a staged ramp — first 3 months we expect ~60% of committed usage while we finish model migration. Can we structure credits/payments to reflect that?
- Procurement will need Net 60 payment terms and a PO flow. Also can you confirm SOC 2 and evidence for security?

We may also request a one-time onboarding subsidy to cover migration costs — can that be folded into the commercials or provided as a service credit?

Can you send a short options matrix and a sample quote for our procurement team? Happy to hop on a 30-min call.

Best,
Alessandro

Option A — 1yr reserve (12 months)
- Commit: $240k (equivalent to current $20k/mo)
- Discount: 10% off list for year 1, conditional on signature and upfront payment of the reserve
- Ramp: first 3 months counted against committed credits but we’ll allow a monthly consumption true-up window at the end of Q1 to reconcile; unused credits in Y1 do not automatically roll but can be applied as a one-time credit at year boundary if you hit >=85% of annual commit.

Option B — 2yr reserve (preferred economics)
- Commit: $240k/year for 2 years (annual invoicing)
- Discounts: 14% Y1, 18% Y2 with standard revenue-recognition language
- Rollover/true-up: 1x annual true-up allowed between Y1 and Y2 to avoid write-offs.

Staged ramp structure (recommended handshake):
- Months 1–3: allow usage up to 60% of committed run-rate without penalties; if total usage is <50% of committed in that window, propose a scoped technical milestone credit (we can apply a one-time onboarding credit to smooth).

Onboarding subsidy: we can propose a service credit applied against the first invoice; need internal approval for size. I’ll loop Ben for the commercial concession and Evelyn for approval on subsidy thresholds.

Procurement items: SOC 2 + security pack is available, Net 45 is our standard on credits for new customers; Net 60 can be evaluated with finance and legal.

Next steps: I’ll pull a clean quote one-pager with 1yr vs 2yr scenarios and a recommended concession. Can we target PO by 11/24 to lock the pricing?

Hi Alessandro —

Appreciate the transparency. We want to make this easy and get Brightpath running on Redwood reliably. Commercial concessions we can offer: 

- Onboarding subsidy: we can provide a $20,000 service credit applied to the first invoice (one-time). 
- Pricing: 12% discount for a 1yr upfront reserve (prepay), 15% for 2yr with annual invoicing and a small additional uplift of 2% if you commit to an expanded usage clause (details below).
- Rollover/true-up: we can support an annual true-up between Y1 and Y2. Operationally: usage is reconciled on the anniversary date; reporting is via your account dashboard + CSV export; finance-to-finance email is accepted as evidence for the reconciliation. Any shortfall after the true-up is payable per the agreed rate.
- Net terms: our standard for new prepay customers is Net 45. We can accept Net 60 for this specific transaction if Brightpath signs an IR (invoice release) addendum and a PO is delivered at time of signature. We’ll need finance review (copy will be CC’d).

Staged uplift incentive (optional): if Brightpath exceeds 120% of committed monthly run-rate in any quarter after Q2, we’ll apply an additional 2% rebate on incremental usage for that quarter (encourages scale).

I’ve attached a slimline quote reflecting the $20k credit and the 12% headline discount (Redwood_Quote_BRP-2026-045.pdf).

Open items: Evelyn to approve the $20k credit and PO/Net60 addendum. Happy to jump on a procurement call.
